value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial real Fourier-coupled sensor model yields an exact all-parameter risk function and establishes when a shared random pivot has strictly more than the matrix-factor-two mean-square error. More importantly, anti-aligned yet everywhere invertible examples make the source alignment bound asymptotically sharp, determining a necessary robustness cost of coupling indices across frequencies. The result informs randomized interpolation and sparse sensor reuse by distinguishing rank/invertibility from mean-square stability; no unproved multistep application is asserted.
